newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin blasts defence minister for "whining".
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin blasts defence minister for "whining".

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who earlier this week suggested a government reshuffle, on Wednesday blasted Defence Minister Igor Rodionov for making public his views that the Russian army was in a catastrophic state.

"The president of the Russian Federation does not approve of remarks made by the defence minister on February 23," said a Kremlin statement. "Whining will not help matters, concrete actions are needed."
"Only military reform can radically improve the situation," said the statement. It said Rodionov and Yeltsin's top defence adviser, Yuri Baturin, should coordinate their positions.
The two defence officials have been squabbling publicly over the course of military reform for several months.

Rodionov has been campaigning to win more funding for the armed forces. "If concrete steps are not taken in the near future -- by 2000 or thereabouts -- our country's defences will be in ruins," he told retired officers on Saturday.

Yeltsin told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday that a cabinet reshuffle might help improve the situation in the country, news which triggered a wave of rumours over which ministers might be sacked. Itar-Tass news agency on Wednesday singled out Rodionov and said he might be sacked in March.
